# Koronos six-case boot-to-target acceptance reference

This reference follows the separation used by Linux distribution builders:
prepare the target root, stage target-specific userspace, build one bootable
medium, test firmware paths, install to a disposable disk, cold-boot that disk,
and retain logs. Debian live-build separates bootstrap/chroot/binary stages;
systemd separates initrd, multi-user, graphical and rescue targets. Koronos
keeps its native boot contract while adopting the staged evidence discipline.

## Immutable six-case matrix

One canonical native Koronos ISO is hashed once. Exactly these six cases must
boot that same byte-for-byte ISO:

| Target | BIOS | UEFI |
|---|---|---|
| Live | live/bios | live/uefi |
| Installer | installer/bios | installer/uefi |
| Recovery | recovery/bios | recovery/uefi |

For each case, the evidence manifest binds the trace to the canonical ISO
SHA-256. The verifier checks firmware identity, ordered kernel-ready ->
CPL3-originated init syscall -> matching nonzero PID readiness, root mount,
a real /tmp write/read round trip, two online CPU identities and measured
overlapping work.

Live additionally requires independent Aurora and Marine desktop-session
traces for each firmware. Installer additionally requires a write token to
survive a cold reboot of the installed disposable disk. Recovery additionally
requires a repair transaction and a matching verified postcondition.

## Evidence marker contract

Markers are not generated by this verifier. Runtime code may emit them only
after the corresponding operation actually succeeds:

- BOOT FIRMWARE: BIOS|UEFI — kernel-derived firmware path, not workflow label.
- VFS ACCEPTANCE: ROOT MOUNTED target=<target> path=/ — successful VFS mount/lookup.
- VFS ACCEPTANCE: TMP WRITE-READ VERIFIED target=<target> path=/tmp — open/write/close/reopen/read/compare through syscalls.
- SMP CPU ONLINE: logical_id=<n> apic_id=<n> — AP startup and per-CPU identity established.
- SMP OVERLAP VERIFIED: cpu_a=<n> cpu_b=<n> overlap_ticks=<n> — measured overlapping work on two CPUs.
- DESKTOP READY: profile=aurora|marine pid=<nonzero> — selected desktop process and compositor/session health checks completed.
- Installer and Recovery transaction markers are defined in the verifier and must be emitted only after a cold-boot persistence check or repair postcondition.

A -smp 2 QEMU argument is not SMP evidence. A desktop manifest is not a
running desktop. An initramfs file is not a mounted VFS. A marker authored
by the kernel before entering CPL3 is not user-originated readiness. Exit 78
remains a hard failure.

## Manifest and invocation

Create evidence/matrix.json with schema koronos-six-case-evidence-v1.
It contains iso_sha256 for the canonical ISO and exactly one case for each
target/firmware pair. Each case contains target, firmware, iso_sha256, trace,
and qemu_exit_code (0 or expected idle timeout 124). Live cases also contain
desktop_traces with aurora and marine paths. Installer and Recovery cases
contain postcondition_trace.

Run:

    python3 tests/boot/verify-six-case-matrix.py \
      --iso build/iso/chimera-ii-os.iso \
      --evidence-dir build/six-case-evidence \
      --report build/six-case-evidence/report.json

The verifier exits zero only for six complete cases. Missing evidence is
BLOCKED, not SKIP or inferred PASS. Its unit tests use synthetic fixtures
only to test verifier behavior; those fixtures are never release evidence.

## Project boundary

ChimeraIIOS uses this gate for its native Koronos ISO. OctavianOS's current
live-image/build.sh creates a Debian/Linux-kernel live edition; that image is
not a native Koronos ISO and cannot satisfy this matrix. Octavian carries the
same verifier beside its vendored Koronos source so native-source acceptance
is consistent, while its Linux live-image tests remain a separate workflow.
Until Octavian builds and boots a canonical native Koronos ISO, its native
six-case status is BLOCKED / NOT BUILT, not a successful Linux live boot.

## Linux workflow comparison

- Debian Live Manual: bootstrap/chroot/binary stages and explicit installer
  integration, rather than mixing package preparation and final media assembly.
- systemd: initrd transitions to multi-user/graphical/rescue targets; Koronos
  maps these to Live, Installer and Recovery target contracts without claiming
  systemd is running inside Koronos.
- Keep build, payload inspection, firmware boot, installed-disk cold boot,
  recovery postcondition, and publication as distinct gates with retained
  artifacts and checksums.
